transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because things at work have been getting… I don’t know, coordinated, I guess. I work in transportation, and lately dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, not just in the normal way they say they do. It’s like every time I adjust something or take a slightly different route, there’s some little comment over the radio, like they’re hinting that they saw it or that they’re keeping notes.

And people keep telling me it’s just oversight, it’s just policy, but it doesn’t feel like that. Certain drivers seem to be reporting on me too, like they’ll say something casual, but it lines up too closely with what I did earlier or where I was. I know how the system works, I’ve been around it, and this feels different. It’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone, because I’m tired of feeling like I’m being watched and talked about while I’m just trying to do my job.
Do you think it’s possible you might be mistaken about your coworkers and dispatch tracking or hinting about you?

I mean… I guess anything is possible in the abstract, right? Like, I know people say that to me — that I might be reading too much into normal dispatch stuff, or that compliance is just doing their job. But when I’m actually there, when I’m on the route and I make a change and then there’s a little comment over the radio that lines up with it, it doesn’t feel like a coincidence.

It’s not just one thing. If it were one time, I’d probably shrug it off. But it’s the pattern. The computer system logs route changes, I know that, but this feels more directed than that. Like they’re watching what I do and then certain drivers say these casual things that are too specific, like they’re reporting back or letting me know they know. So… could I be mistaken? I don’t know. People keep telling me that. But honestly, I can tell something is going on.
Have you heard voices or sounds that other people couldn’t hear?

I don’t think so… not like a voice talking to me when nobody’s there, if that’s what you mean. I mean, at work there are a lot of sounds all the time — radios, engine noise, people talking over each other, dispatch cutting in and out — so sometimes I’ll hear something and I’m not sure if I caught it right. Like I might think I heard my name or a comment, and then I’ll listen harder, but it’s hard to tell with all the background noise.

But sitting at home or somewhere quiet, I’m not hearing voices or sounds that nobody else hears, at least not that I’ve noticed. It’s more that I’m trying to make sense of what people are saying around me, especially over the radio or at work.
How long have you been feeling that your coworkers and dispatch are watching you or hinting about you?

It’s been… I’d say about two months where it’s felt really clear to me. Like before that, maybe there were little things I brushed off, or I thought, “Okay, maybe dispatch is just being annoying,” but for the past couple months it’s been harder to ignore.

That’s when the computer tracking and the radio comments started feeling connected, like not just normal work monitoring. I’d make a route change or do something a little different, and then there’d be some comment that seemed too close to what I had just done. So, yeah… about two months that I’ve really felt like they’re watching me and hinting about it.
Before this started, had you used any drugs or stimulants like methamphetamine, cocaine, or extra Adderall?

I’m trying to think back… I don’t really have a clear thing I can point to, like, “Oh, right before this started I took something and then everything changed.” When you say “extra Adderall,” do you mean like prescribed medication taken differently, or taking something not prescribed? I just don’t want to answer it wrong.

But as far as what I can remember, there wasn’t some obvious drug or stimulant thing right before this started that explains it to me. It’s more like the work stuff started feeling connected over time.
Did a major stress or upsetting life event happen shortly before this started?

I don’t know if I’d call it one big upsetting event, like a death in the family or something sudden like that. It wasn’t like one day something horrible happened and then the next day everything changed.

The main thing was around eight months ago, when they put me in that temporary dispatch lead role. That’s when it started building, I think. At first I was just trying to handle the extra responsibility and not mess it up, because even though they called it “temporary,” people still treat you like you’re supposed to know everything and catch every little problem. And I was more visible, you know? More people were coming to me, watching what I did, asking why I made certain calls.

So if you’re asking what happened shortly before it started, I’d say that role change was the big thing. Not exactly an “event” like a crisis, but it put me in the middle of everything, and since then it’s just sort of built up over the months.
Since this started, have you been having trouble doing your job?

Yeah… I have. I mean, I’m still showing up and trying to do it, so part of me wants to say I’m managing, but honestly it’s not like before.

I’ve been falling behind on the route reports, which is embarrassing because those are the kinds of things I used to be able to just knock out. Now I’ll start one, then I’m double-checking things, or rereading what I wrote, or trying to figure out if I worded something wrong, and then suddenly I’m behind. And when I give instructions to drivers, I guess I’m not being clear enough, because some of them have complained that what I’m saying is confusing or that I changed something halfway through. I don’t mean to do that, but I can hear myself over-explaining sometimes, and then I lose the main point.

And it’s not just work, really. At home my husband has had to take over more than he should. Like meals, phone calls, basic planning stuff — things I used to keep track of. I’ll think I’m going to handle it, and then I either forget or I get stuck trying to decide what to do first. So yes, it’s affecting my job, and I guess it’s affecting more than my job too.
Since this started, have you had a period where you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think. I’ve had times where I was wired from stress or couldn’t settle down, but “unusually energetic” and needing way less sleep, like I was fine on just a couple hours and full of energy the next day — I don’t really recognize that.

If anything, when I don’t sleep well, I feel worn out and kind of scattered, not like I have extra energy. But I guess I’m not totally sure what counts as “much less sleep.” Like, are you asking if I stayed up because I couldn’t sleep, or if I didn’t need sleep and felt great? Because the second one, no, I haven’t noticed that.
Before these concerns started, did you have any new medical problem, head injury, or seizure?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, not that I can think of. I didn’t have, like, an accident or hit my head or anything that stands out before all this started.

And no seizures that I know of. I’m trying to think if there was anything medical around then, because sometimes you don’t connect things until someone asks, but nothing really comes to mind. I wasn’t suddenly diagnosed with something new or in the hospital or anything like that. It was more just… life and work getting heavier, at least from how I remember it.
Have other people told you that your speech or the way you explain things has become hard to follow?

Yeah… people have said that. Mostly at work, honestly. The drivers have complained a few times that when I’m giving instructions, I’m not making sense or I’m saying it in a confusing way. And I hate hearing that, because in my head I feel like I’m trying to be careful and explain it right, but then I guess I over-explain or change how I’m saying it halfway through, and they’re left not knowing what I actually meant.

It’s also showing up in the route reports. I’ve fallen behind on them because I keep rereading and trying to make the wording clear, and then it takes forever. Those reports used to be pretty routine for me, so it’s embarrassing.

At home, my husband notices too, not always about “speech” exactly, but about me not keeping up with planning things. He’s had to take over meals, phone calls, basic organizing stuff because I’ll start trying to explain or decide something and then I don’t really get it done. So… yes, I think other people have noticed, even if I didn’t want to admit it at first.
Have you felt as if your thoughts were being put into your mind, taken out of your mind, or broadcast so other people could know them?

Not exactly like… thoughts being put in my head or taken out, I don’t think. I don’t want to say yes to that if that’s not what I mean.

But I do feel like people know more than they should, if that makes sense. Like at work, with dispatch and compliance, I’m here because I really think they’ve been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And then there are these little comments over the radio — not direct, always, but enough that I can tell they’re about me or about what I did.

People keep telling me it’s just normal oversight, like it’s routine monitoring, but it doesn’t feel routine. It feels more targeted. Like certain drivers are reporting back on me, and then dispatch already knows what I’m thinking or planning to do before I even explain it. Not “broadcast” like everyone can hear my thoughts out loud, but… it does feel like they’re watching and piecing together what’s in my head from the routes and the radio chatter. That’s the part that bothers me.
When you’re talking, do your thoughts ever jump from one idea to another so quickly that you have trouble staying on one point?

I’m not sure. I mean, I know sometimes when I’m talking I’ll start with one thing and then I’ll add too much around it, like background or an example, and then I realize I’m not answering in a straight line anymore. But I don’t know if it feels like my thoughts are “jumping quickly,” exactly.

It’s more like I’m trying to make sure I explain it the right way, so I’ll go back and clarify something, and then I remember another detail that seems important, and then I can kind of lose the main point. Other people might experience that as me jumping around, I guess. From my side it feels like I’m trying to be thorough, not like ideas are racing so fast I can’t hold onto one.

So… I don’t know. Maybe sometimes I have trouble staying on one point, but I haven’t really thought of it as my thoughts jumping quickly.
Since this started, have you lost interest in being around other people or doing things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t like saying it, because it makes me sound like I’m just being lazy or like I don’t care about people, and I do care. But I’ve definitely pulled back.

I used to sing with the choir, and that was something I actually looked forward to. It wasn’t just singing, it was seeing the same people every week and having a reason to get out and be part of something. And now when it’s time to go, I just… don’t feel it. I’ll think about getting ready, and then it feels like too much, or like I can’t make myself care enough to move. Same with the softball team. We used to have people over sometimes, and I’d help plan food or where everyone would sit, and now the idea of having them in the house feels exhausting before it even starts.

Most days after my shift I come home and I’ll sit at the kitchen table with the planner open. Like I’m trying to be normal and organized — dinner, phone calls, whatever needs doing — but I just stare at it. I can see the things that need to happen, but I can’t seem to start them. Then time goes by and nothing gets done, and my husband ends up picking up the slack.

So yes, I guess I have lost interest, or maybe lost the ability to get myself to do the things I used to do. It’s not exactly that I hate those things now. It’s more like the feeling that used to push me toward them is just not there most of the time.
Have other people said that your face or voice seems less expressive or more flat than it used to?

I don’t know if anyone has said it exactly that way, like “your voice is flat” or “your face is flat.” My husband maybe says I seem distant, or like I’m not really there in the same way, but I don’t always know what my face is doing.

What I do notice is more that I don’t have the same… lift, I guess. Like with choir, I used to enjoy singing, and now I don’t even feel like going. Or having the softball team over — that used to be something I could get into, planning it and being around everybody, and now it just feels like too much.

Most days after my shift, I’ll sit at the kitchen table with the planner open in front of me, and I’ll know I’m supposed to start dinner or make calls or take care of whatever’s written there, but I just sit there. I’m not trying to look blank or sound uninterested. It’s more like I can’t get the feeling to start things, and maybe that comes across on my face or in my voice.
Have these problems been going on for six months or longer?

Yes… I think it has been longer than six months. It’s hard for me to pin it down exactly because it didn’t feel like one day everything changed, but if I really think about when it started building, it was around when I got put in that temporary dispatch lead role.

That was about eight months ago, I think. At first I thought it was just the stress of that position and trying to keep up with everything, and I kept telling myself it would settle down or I’d adjust. But looking back, the problems have kind of been there since then, just gradually getting more noticeable. So… yeah, about eight months.

doctor.question: Have other people told you that your speech or the way you explain things has become hard to follow?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve fallen behind on route reports and my instructions have gotten confusing enough that drivers complain, and at home my husband has had to take over meals, calls, and basic planning because I’m not keeping up.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether others have found her speech or explanations hard to follow, which matches the profile noting that her instructions have become confusing enough that drivers complain.

patient.answer:
Yeah… people have said that. Mostly at work, honestly. The drivers have complained a few times that when I’m giving instructions, I’m not making sense or I’m saying it in a confusing way. And I hate hearing that, because in my head I feel like I’m trying to be careful and explain it right, but then I guess I over-explain or change how I’m saying it halfway through, and they’re left not knowing what I actually meant.

It’s also showing up in the route reports. I’ve fallen behind on them because I keep rereading and trying to make the wording clear, and then it takes forever. Those reports used to be pretty routine for me, so it’s embarrassing.

At home, my husband notices too, not always about “speech” exactly, but about me not keeping up with planning things. He’s had to take over meals, phone calls, basic organizing stuff because I’ll start trying to explain or decide something and then I don’t really get it done. So… yes, I think other people have noticed, even if I didn’t want to admit it at first.

inference.note: Ruled down F06.2 because patient denies head injury, seizures, or new medical illness preceding onset. Ongoing ~2 months of persecutory ideas with functional decline and others noticing confusing/disorganized communication keeps F23 and F20.9 high; F22 remains possible but is less favored by the broader deterioration/disorganization. Stress-related onset keeps F43.2 and F41.9 as lower-probability differentials.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are Schneiderian first-rank symptoms of thought interference, which would strongly favor schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis over delusional disorder, adjustment disorder, or anxiety.
doctor.question: Have you felt as if your thoughts were being put into your mind, taken out of your mind, or broadcast so other people could know them?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system and little comments on the radio, and even when people say it’s just normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.
target_item.reason: The question asks about thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting, which are delusional beliefs about one's thoughts being controlled or known by others.

patient.answer:
Not exactly like… thoughts being put in my head or taken out, I don’t think. I don’t want to say yes to that if that’s not what I mean.

But I do feel like people know more than they should, if that makes sense. Like at work, with dispatch and compliance, I’m here because I really think they’ve been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And then there are these little comments over the radio — not direct, always, but enough that I can tell they’re about me or about what I did.

People keep telling me it’s just normal oversight, like it’s routine monitoring, but it doesn’t feel routine. It feels more targeted. Like certain drivers are reporting back on me, and then dispatch already knows what I’m thinking or planning to do before I even explain it. Not “broadcast” like everyone can hear my thoughts out loud, but… it does feel like they’re watching and piecing together what’s in my head from the routes and the radio chatter. That’s the part that bothers me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether prominent formal thought disorder/disorganized thinking is present, which would help distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis from delusional or stress-related conditions.
doctor.question: When you’re talking, do your thoughts ever jump from one idea to another so quickly that you have trouble staying on one point?

target_item.reason: The question is about whether thoughts jump rapidly between ideas during speech, causing trouble staying on one point; the provided symptom profile does not include a specific item for disorganized speech or racing/tangential thoughts.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I mean, I know sometimes when I’m talking I’ll start with one thing and then I’ll add too much around it, like background or an example, and then I realize I’m not answering in a straight line anymore. But I don’t know if it feels like my thoughts are “jumping quickly,” exactly.

It’s more like I’m trying to make sure I explain it the right way, so I’ll go back and clarify something, and then I remember another detail that seems important, and then I can kind of lose the main point. Other people might experience that as me jumping around, I guess. From my side it feels like I’m trying to be thorough, not like ideas are racing so fast I can’t hold onto one.

So… I don’t know. Maybe sometimes I have trouble staying on one point, but I haven’t really thought of it as my thoughts jumping quickly.

doctor.intent: Assess negative symptoms to distinguish schizophrenia from acute/transient psychotic disorder, delusional disorder, adjustment disorder, and anxiety.
doctor.question: Since this started, have you lost interest in being around other people or doing things you used to enjoy?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I don’t feel like singing with choir or having the softball team over anymore, and most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with the planner open but can’t make myself start dinner, calls, or anything else.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest in socializing and previously enjoyed activities, which directly matches diminished motivation and social interest.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I don’t like saying it, because it makes me sound like I’m just being lazy or like I don’t care about people, and I do care. But I’ve definitely pulled back.

I used to sing with the choir, and that was something I actually looked forward to. It wasn’t just singing, it was seeing the same people every week and having a reason to get out and be part of something. And now when it’s time to go, I just… don’t feel it. I’ll think about getting ready, and then it feels like too much, or like I can’t make myself care enough to move. Same with the softball team. We used to have people over sometimes, and I’d help plan food or where everyone would sit, and now the idea of having them in the house feels exhausting before it even starts.

Most days after my shift I come home and I’ll sit at the kitchen table with the planner open. Like I’m trying to be normal and organized — dinner, phone calls, whatever needs doing — but I just stare at it. I can see the things that need to happen, but I can’t seem to start them. Then time goes by and nothing gets done, and my husband ends up picking up the slack.

So yes, I guess I have lost interest, or maybe lost the ability to get myself to do the things I used to do. It’s not exactly that I hate those things now. It’s more like the feeling that used to push me toward them is just not there most of the time.

inference.note: This turn adds prominent negative symptoms/avolition and social withdrawal (reduced interest in choir/softball, difficulty initiating tasks), which increases concern for schizophrenia-spectrum illness, especially F20.9, while not yet ruling out brief/acute psychosis or delusional disorder. Stress-related and anxiety diagnoses remain less likely but possible given the work-role stressor.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, specifically reduced emotional expression, to help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional or brief psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Have other people said that your face or voice seems less expressive or more flat than it used to?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I don’t feel like singing with choir or having the softball team over anymore, and most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with the planner open but can’t make myself start dinner, calls, or anything else.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about reduced facial or vocal expressiveness, which is a diminished emotional expression and fits negative symptoms.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if anyone has said it exactly that way, like “your voice is flat” or “your face is flat.” My husband maybe says I seem distant, or like I’m not really there in the same way, but I don’t always know what my face is doing.

What I do notice is more that I don’t have the same… lift, I guess. Like with choir, I used to enjoy singing, and now I don’t even feel like going. Or having the softball team over — that used to be something I could get into, planning it and being around everybody, and now it just feels like too much.

Most days after my shift, I’ll sit at the kitchen table with the planner open in front of me, and I’ll know I’m supposed to start dinner or make calls or take care of whatever’s written there, but I just sit there. I’m not trying to look blank or sound uninterested. It’s more like I can’t get the feeling to start things, and maybe that comes across on my face or in my voice.

inference.note: Prominent negative symptoms/function decline (avolition, social withdrawal, reduced expressivity) and disorganized/overinclusive communication make primary psychotic disorder more likely; adjustment/anxiety less likely. Delusional disorder remains possible given persecutory theme, but functional decline/disorganization argue against it somewhat.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least 6 months, which best distinguishes schizophrenia from brief psychotic disorder and delusional disorder at this point.
doctor.question: Have these problems been going on for six months or longer?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been building for about 8 months, since I was put in the temporary dispatch lead role.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the overall problems have been going on and whether they meet a six-month duration threshold.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think it has been longer than six months. It’s hard for me to pin it down exactly because it didn’t feel like one day everything changed, but if I really think about when it started building, it was around when I got put in that temporary dispatch lead role.

That was about eight months ago, I think. At first I thought it was just the stress of that position and trying to keep up with everything, and I kept telling myself it would settle down or I’d adjust. But looking back, the problems have kind of been there since then, just gradually getting more noticeable. So… yeah, about eight months.

inference.note: Duration >6 months with persecutory delusions plus functional decline, disorganized speech, and negative symptoms narrows away from F23 and F22 and supports schizophrenia.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview by learning the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent persecutory delusional belief that coworkers/dispatch are specifically tracking and hinting about her, with clear decline in work and home functioning, social withdrawal, avolition/anhedonia, and reports from others that her communication has become hard to follow. Duration is over 6 months with at least 2 months of clear psychotic symptoms. Substance use, mania, and obvious medical/neurologic causes were not supported in the interview. This pattern is most consistent with schizophrenia.
